transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Uh… mostly work stuff. I’ve been making mistakes I really shouldn’t be making on sales reports—copying the wrong numbers from the team dashboard, or missing a line in a procedure I was supposed to check. Even when I think I went over it, something gets missed. It’s been… frustrating.
When did you first start noticing these kinds of mistakes and trouble focusing—has this been a lifelong pattern, or did it start more recently, like in the past few weeks or months?

I think it’s been around a long time. My mom still brings up notes from elementary school… teachers saying I rushed through work, lost homework, talked out of turn, couldn’t stay in my seat unless they kept reminding me. So, not really just the last few months.
Besides the trouble focusing, do you currently notice yourself feeling restless, fidgety, or acting impulsively—like interrupting others or making quick decisions without thinking them through?
Yeah… I do get restless. Like in a long meeting, I feel kind of… buzzing inside. I’ll shift around a lot, tap my foot, or try to find some excuse to stand up for a minute.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you noticed feeling persistently sad, down, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy?
Not really, no. I mean… I get frustrated, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been persistently sad or lost interest in things.
Do you often find yourself getting into arguments, breaking rules, or acting aggressively toward others—either now or when you were younger?
No… not really. I mean, I can get annoyed or impatient, but I don’t think I’ve been aggressive or, like, someone who breaks rules a lot. Not that I can remember.
Do you often find yourself deliberately defying or arguing with authority figures, like bosses or teachers, or losing your temper more easily than others might in similar situations?

Not really. I mean, I don’t love being told what to do, but I don’t think I’m deliberately defying people or getting into it with bosses or anything. I can get irritated, but… not more than most people, I don’t think.
Do you notice these same problems with focus, restlessness, or impulsivity affecting you outside of work too—like at home, in relationships, or in social situations?

Yeah… it does. I mean, work is where it’s gotten noticed the most—my manager actually put it in a formal review.

At home, it causes problems too. People get frustrated because they feel like they can’t count on me to follow through on things.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a longstanding (since childhood, corroborated by school records) pattern of inattention (careless mistakes, losing items, difficulty sustaining focus, forgetfulness) combined with hyperactive-impulsive symptoms (restlessness, fidgeting, need to move during meetings). These symptoms are present across multiple settings (work and home) and cause functional impairment (formal work review, relationship strain). No evidence of mood episode (denies persistent sadness/anhedonia), conduct disorder (denies aggression, rule-breaking), or oppositional defiant disorder (denies defiance, excessive irritability toward authority). This presentation with both inattentive and hyperactive-impulsive features supports ADHD, combined presentation (F90.0).
